land.text: 'the territories to the north of the Balkan Mountains' that the Byzantines ceded in the 681 treaty (Moesia, 'Bulgar conquest of Moesia' on the Asparukh page)

predecessors.note: 681: 'In 681, the Byzantines were compelled to sign a humiliating peace treaty'. The Byzantine dossier records the same hand-over as a loss in 681.

land.text: Old Great Bulgaria's last Cliopatria shape (674-681, the Black Sea steppe north of the Danube delta) lies wholly inside the First Bulgarian Empire's first shape

predecessors.note: Asparukh page: 'the state disintegrated under Khazar attack in 668' and Asparukh 'settled in the Danube Delta'. No page opened says the steppe land passed to Asparukh; Cliopatria carries it over. See notes.

land.text: the last Cliopatria shape (1015-1017), the remaining Bulgarian land from Ohrid and Bitola to the Albanian mountains: 'Bulgaria was annexed by the Byzantine Empire' in 1018 and became the theme of Bulgaria

successors.note: The Serbian and Duklja lands that Samuel had held (Raska, Montenegro) are inside this shape but their fate in 1018 is not given by the pages opened. The Second Bulgarian Empire (1185) is a later restoration, not a successor of 1018.

capitals.name: Pliska
capitals.note: Infobox 'Pliska (681-893)'; the Simeon page: an assembly 'moved the Bulgarian capital from Pliska to Preslav' (893). Asparukh page: credited with 'building the major centres of Pliska and Drastar' but not named as capital there.

capitals.name: Preslav (Veliki Preslav)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Preslav (893-968/972)'. Sviatoslav's Rus' took the city in 969 and the Byzantines stormed it on 13 April 971, taking Tsar Boris II to Constantinople; the court then had no capital until the infobox's Skopje (972).

capitals.name: Ohrid
capitals.note: Infobox 'Ohrid (992-1015)'; Samuel page: 'Samuel moved the capital from Skopje to Ohrid'. Basil II's army 'took the capital Ohrid and burned the imperial palaces' in 1015 (Ivan Vladislav page) and Bulgarian forces retook it.

capitals.name: Bitola
capitals.note: Infobox 'Bitola (1015-1018)'; Ivan Vladislav page: reconstruction began in October 1015 'including the fortress at Bitola'.

rulers.name: Asparukh
rulers.note: Infobox '681-700: Asparuh'; the Asparukh page: 'frequently end his reign in 700 or 701', Moskov's chronology 668-695.

rulers.name: Tervel
rulers.note: Infobox '700-721'. No ruler is named on the pages opened between 721 and 777.

rulers.name: Krum
rulers.note: Krum page: 'from sometime between 796 and 803 until his death in 814'; 'died 13 April 814'. Infobox 803-814.

rulers.name: Malamir
rulers.note: Reign years derived: Omurtag died 831 (Omurtag page) and Presian's infobox reign begins 836, with Malamir as his predecessor; the Presian page gives no dates for Malamir.

rulers.name: Boris I
rulers.note: 852 to abdication in 889; he returned in 893 to depose his son.

rulers.name: Vladimir-Rasate
rulers.note: 'In 889 Boris abdicated'; Vladimir was deposed and blinded in 893 (Simeon page).

rulers.name: Simeon I
rulers.note: 'Reign: 893 - 27 May 927'; emperor from the late-913 recognition.

rulers.name: Peter I
rulers.note: Reign began 27 May 927; abdicated after a stroke in 969 and died 30 January 970.

rulers.name: Boris II
rulers.note: Seized by Sviatoslav and ruling only nominally; stripped of his insignia and taken to Constantinople after the Byzantine capture of Preslav in 971 (Sviatoslav page). The Byzantine-Bulgarian wars page gives his death in 977; no page opened dates the succession of Roman or Samuel's rise before 997.

rulers.name: Samuel
rulers.note: Infobox '997-1014'; chosen emperor in 997 after Roman died in captivity; died 6 October 1014. He led the Cometopuli state from 976 on as commander (Samuel page, 14 June 976).

rulers.name: Gavril Radomir
rulers.note: Succeeded Samuel; murdered by Ivan Vladislav in 1015 (lead: 'October 1015', body text: late summer).

rulers.name: Ivan Vladislav
rulers.note: Infobox '1015-1018'; killed under the walls of Dyrrhachium in February 1018 (Ivan Vladislav page).

correction.text: unchanged shape for 681; the state's birth year is 681

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first shape begins in 682 but the Bulgarian state is dated 681 (infobox: recognised by Byzantium in 681, Ongal in 680). Same shape as 682.

Moesia, Dobruja and the delta are attested (Asparukh page: 'the Bulgar conquest of Moesia'; main page: the lands north of the Balkan Mountains). The steppe north of the Danube to the Dnieper (Odessa, Mykolayiv, Kherson, Muntenia, Oltenia) is not: the shape inherits Old Great Bulgaria's last shape (674-681) and the Asparukh page says that state 'disintegrated under Khazar attack in 668' and gives no northern or eastern limit. The Dnieper is attested only for Krum's and Omurtag's reigns. Unverified for 682-805; treat as soft. No infobox area for 682.
Zagore south of the Balkan Mountains is added in 705 (ledger 705); the 716 agreement 'defined the borders' but the page names no line. Same unverified steppe as 682.

The Avar lands are added (ledger 805): Krum's state is 'spreading from the middle Danube to the Dnieper' and the Tisza is the northwest limit. Transylvania is doubtful: the Krum page finds 'no sign that Krum's military campaign touched Transylvania' while Cliopatria holds 25% of it; kept, soft.

The Serdica basin (809) and the Black Sea coast and Yambol plain (812) are in; Adrianople (813-815) is not, and Plovdiv stays outside as the 815 treaty required ('without including Plovdiv'). Border from Debeltos along the Erkesia trench to the Maritsa at Kalugerovo.
Part of the Danube-Tisza fringe (Backa, Pest county) is dropped, a loss bridged to the 818 Slavic revolt in the west (ledger 825, confidence 1).

Omurtag's fleet 'restored Bulgarian control over portions of southeastern Pannonia' in 827 (and 829); the shape starts in 830 and reaches Slavonia and Zagreb (15.3 E), more than 'portions' and more than any page bounds. Kept as drawn, soft in the west.
Pannonian land returns to the Franks (page silent, ledger 840); Plovdiv is in (Malamir, 831-836). Same steppe as before.

Presian's Macedonia (ledger 850, confidence 1). Infobox area 400,000 km2 in 850 against 428,320 km2 here (ratio 1.07): consistent. The 855-856 loss of Plovdiv, Zagora and the Burgas ports is not drawn; see the new keyframe for 856-863. This shape holds 850-855.

correction.text: the 860 shape without Philippopolis, Zagora and the ports round the Gulf of Burgas, 856-863

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Boris lost Philippopolis (Plovdiv), the region of Zagora, and the ports around the Gulf of Burgas' to Michael III and Bardas in 855-856; Zagora came back in 864 (ledger 864). Cliopatria's 860 shape keeps them. Whether Plovdiv and the Burgas ports returned with Zagora is not on the page; after 864 they are kept as Cliopatria draws them.

correction.text: unchanged shape; it holds from 864 to 865, the 856-863 years take the new keyframe

keyframe_review.note: Years only: this shape is right for 864-865 (Zagora back); for 860-863 the new keyframe for 856 applies.

Area equal to the previous shape within 0.1% (about a cell): no border moves; Cliopatria re-draws the same frontier. Boris I page: 'the skilful diplomacy of Boris I' kept the realm; the 870 council gave Bulgaria its own archbishopric; in 886 'Boris' governor of Belgrade' is attested, so the Danube-Sava frontier stands.
Same frontier as the previous shape, area within 0.1%. Boris I page: no territorial change dated between 864 and 893; Belgrade held by a Bulgarian governor in 886.
Same frontier as the previous shape, area within 0.1%. Boris I page: no territorial change dated between 864 and 893; Belgrade held by a Bulgarian governor in 886.
Same frontier as the previous shape, area within 0.1%. Boris I page: no territorial change dated between 864 and 893; Belgrade held by a Bulgarian governor in 886.
Same frontier as the previous shape, area within 0.1%. Boris I page: no territorial change dated between 864 and 893; Belgrade held by a Bulgarian governor in 886.

The 896 peace gave 'an area between the Black Sea and Strandza' (ledger 896), drawn here for 896-897 only; the shape also drops the Black Sea steppe (Odessa, Mykolayiv, Kherson, Budjak), for which no page opened gives a date or a holder (ledger 896, confidence 1). Kept.
The steppe is back (the Bulgarians 'attacked and routed the Hungarians', undated) and the Strandza strip is gone; neither move is dated by a page (ledger 898, confidence 1).

correction.text: unchanged shape; it holds 900-903, the 904-910 years take the new keyframe

keyframe_review.note: Years only: this shape holds 900-903. It drops Banat, Transylvania and the plain to the Tisza (ledger 900, confidence 1, page silent on Bulgarian rule there) and the Magyars occupy Pannonia 'in 900'. For 904-910 the new keyframe for 904 applies.

correction.text: the 900 shape plus southern Albania, without the plain within 20 km of Thessaloniki

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 904 treaty ceded 'all Slavic-inhabited lands in modern southern Macedonia and southern Albania' and the border ran 'some 20 kilometres north of Thessaloniki' (the 850-900 shapes reach the Thessalonian plain). Cliopatria adds the west only in 911.

Adds central and northern Albania, Raska and Kosovo to the 904 frontier (ledger 911, page silent). The Simeon page: 'Bulgaria spread over a territory between the Aegean, the Adriatic and the Black seas'. Thracian conquests of 914-922 (Adrianople, Bizye) are not drawn; the contest zone stands for them.

Years only: holds 922-924; Serbia was annexed at the end of 924, so 925 takes the new keyframe. Infobox area 287,000 km2 in 925 against 348,411 km2 here (ratio 1.21); the 926 shape (420,684 km2, ratio 1.47) includes Serbia.

correction.text: the 926 shape for the single year 925

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Bulgaria annexed Serbia directly' at the end of 924, so 925 already has the 926 shape (the 922 shape plus the whole Serbian principality).

Years only: holds 926-932; 'Caslav escaped the Bulgarian capital Preslav in 933' and Serbia regained independence, so 933-935 take the new keyframe. The Croatian invasion of 926 was 'checked' (main page), so Bosnia and Dalmatia are not Bulgarian; the shape reaches Bosnia only through the Serbian principality's own Cliopatria shape.
New keyframe: Serbia is independent again from 933; the Bulgarian frontier returns to the 936 shape.

Frontier 'restored to those defined in treaties of 897 and 904' (927 peace). Infobox area 240,000 km2 for 950 against 355,589 km2 for the 947 shape (ratio 1.48): within a factor of two, shape kept; the infobox may leave out the Albanian and Raska fringes. The shape keeps 43 cells that the 922 shape did not hold, unexplained.

No border move on the Peter I page between 936 and 968: 'a period of 40 years of peaceful relations' with Byzantium; area within 1% of the previous shape. Infobox 950: 240,000 km2 against 355,589 km2 (ratio 1.48).
Same frontier as the previous shape (area within 1%); no territorial change is dated on the Peter I page before the Rus' invasion of 968.
Same frontier as the previous shape (area within 1%); no territorial change is dated on the Peter I page before the Rus' invasion of 968.

The Rus' invaded in 968 and the Byzantines annexed the east in 971; this shape already omits the Dobruja, the north-east, Thrace and the north bank. It stands for 970-971 with the Rus' occupation hatched and from 971 as the rump 'west of the Iskar', which 'remained free'. Area 226,160 km2.
Samuel's Cometopuli state holds the west; the shape drops Oltenia and Syrmia (ledger 980, page silent). 'The lands to the west of the Iskar River remained free' after 971.

Samuel's realm at its height: Epirus and Durres (989), Thessaly, Moesia and the old capitals again (c. 991), Duklja (997/998). The shape draws all of it from 990; the Duklja part is dated 997 or 998 by the pages. The Samuel page: his realm held 'most of the Balkans (with the notable exception of Thrace)'.
Adds Syrmia on the Danube (ledger 1000, page silent); otherwise Samuel's realm as in 990.
After Basil II's campaigns: Preslav and Pliska (1000), Macedonian towns (1001), Thessalian towns (1001-1002), Vidin (1003, the shape drops it only in 1010).
Skopje (1004) and Dyrrhachium (1005) are lost; the rest of the loss is page silent (ledger 1010, confidence 1). Unverified for 1006-1013.

correction.text: the 1015 shape plus the district of Pernik, which withstood Basil II in 1016

keyframe_review.note: Ivan Vladislav's rump. The Ivan Vladislav page has the Bulgarians withstand an 88-day siege of Pernik in spring 1016 ('the 88-day siege was a failure'), so the Sofia basin round Pernik is not Byzantine before 1018; this shape omits it. The researcher's reading adds a 40 km circle round Pernik.

correction.text: the 1017 shape plus the district of Pernik for the last year

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria ends in 1017 but Bulgarian forces held out until 1018: Ivan Vladislav fell at Dyrrhachium in February and his sons 'surrendered by the end of 1018'.

region.text: 'the territories to the north of the Balkan Mountains' ceded in 681: Moesia, and the Danube delta where Asparukh's Bulgars had settled

ledger.note: 681: Asparukh's Bulgars found the Bulgarian state between the Danube and the Balkan Mountains. 'It was founded in 680-681 after a group of Bulgars' defeated 'the Byzantine army led by Constantine IV'; 'In 681, the Byzantines were compelled to sign a humiliating peace treaty' and 'to cede the territories to the north of the Balkan Mountains'; infobox 'New Bulgarian state recognized by Eastern Roman Empire: 681', 'Battle of Ongal: 680'. The Asparukh page: 'Asparuh's victory led to the Bulgar conquest of Moesia'. Dobruja (the delta) is the researcher's reading of where the Bulgars had settled.

region.text: 'the Zagore region of Northern Thrace', south of the Balkan Mountains; the four provinces are the researcher's reading, matching the land Cliopatria's 705 shape adds

ledger.note: 705: Tervel is rewarded with Zagore. 'In 705 he assisted the deposed Byzantine Emperor Justinian II in regaining his throne' 'in return for the Zagore region of Northern Thrace', 'the first expansion of Bulgaria to the south of the Balkan mountains.' (A 716 agreement 'defined the borders' without the page naming the line.)

region.text: the Avar lands between the Danube and the Tisza (Banat, Vojvodina, the Great Hungarian Plain east of the Danube), as Cliopatria's 806 shape adds them to the 705 shape

ledger.note: c. 805: Krum destroys the Avar Khaganate and takes its eastern lands. 'Around 805, Krum defeated the Avar Khaganate to destroy the remainder of the Avars' and 'advanced northward into the Tisza region'; the main page: 'Between 804 and 806 the Bulgarian armies thoroughly eliminated the Avar Khaganate', 'a border with the Frankish Empire was established along the middle Danube or Tisza.' The Krum page finds 'no sign that Krum's military campaign touched Transylvania' and the Hungarian-conquest page has only 'intermittent influence' there from c. 822, yet Cliopatria's 806 shape holds a quarter of Transylvania.

region.text: Serdica and the Sofia basin

ledger.note: 809: Krum takes Serdica (Sofia). 'In 809 Krum besieged and forced the surrender of Serdica, slaughtering the garrison of 6,000.' The main page: 'in 809 captured the important city of Serdica (modern Sofia).'

region.text: Byzantine Thrace round Adrianople, Mesembria and Develt

ledger.note: 812: Krum carries the war into Byzantine Thrace. 'In 812 Krum invaded Byzantine Thrace, taking Develt'; autumn 812 Mesembria; 813 Versinikia (22 June) and a siege of Adrianople; Nikephoros I had taken Pliska on 20 July 811 and was trapped at the Varbitsa Pass on 26 July. The fighting runs to the 815 treaty.

region.text: Develt (Debeltos) and Mesembria on the Black Sea coast, and the Thracian plain to the Erkesia trench

ledger.note: 812: Develt and Mesembria fall to Krum. 'In 812 Krum invaded Byzantine Thrace, taking Develt'; 'besieged and captured Mesembria' in 'the autumn of 812'. The main page: 'in 812 moved the war towards Thrace, capturing the key Black Sea port of Messembria'. The Yambol plain is the researcher's reading of the land between Debeltos and the Erkesia trench border of 815 that Cliopatria's 814 shape adds.

region.text: Adrianople and its district

ledger.note: 813: Krum seizes Adrianople. 'defeating the Byzantines once more at Versinikia in 813', 'the Bulgarians pillaged Eastern Thrace and seized the important city of Adrianople', 'resettling its 10,000 inhabitants' across the Danube. The Krum page has only that Adrianople 'resisted, and was besieged by Krum's brother'. The city is outside the border of 815, so it is an occupation, not a gain.

region.text: Adrianople

ledger.note: 815: Adrianople is outside the new frontier. The thirty-year treaty set 'the border along the Erkesia trench between Debeltos on the Black Sea' 'and the valley of the Maritsa River at Kalugerovo'; the page does not say the city was returned, which is the researcher's reading of that line.

region.text: Byzantine Thrace

ledger.note: 815: Omurtag makes the thirty years' peace with Byzantium. '30-year peace treaty with the Byzantines in 815'; it 'began on the Black Sea coast near Debelt' and ran to the Maritsa and Rhodopes 'without including Plovdiv within Bulgaria's borders'.

region.text: the western fringe of the Avar lands (Backa and the Danube-Tisza interfluve) that Cliopatria's 825 shape no longer holds

ledger.note: c. 825: Cliopatria's shape drops part of the Danube-Tisza lands in the west. Page silent on a loss: Omurtag page: 'In 818 the Slavic tribes of the Timocani, Abodrites, and Braničevci' rose against Bulgarian control in the west and sought Frankish backing; 824-826 diplomacy with the Franks failed. The shape change (about 47 cells, Backa and Pest county) is bridged to that revolt.

region.text: 'portions of southeastern Pannonia': Slavonia, Syrmia and the Sava-Drava lands, as Cliopatria's 830 shape adds them

ledger.note: 827: Omurtag's fleet on the Danube and the Drava recovers southeastern Pannonia. 'In 827 he sent a fleet along the Danube and the Drava' and 'restored Bulgarian control over portions of southeastern Pannonia'; 'Similar events took place again in 829'. The main page: 'the northwestern boundaries with the Frankish Empire were firmly settled along the middle Danube by 827' and 'To the west the Bulgarians were in control of Belgrade'. Cliopatria's 830 shape reaches Slavonia and Zagreb, more than 'portions'.

region.text: Philippopolis (Plovdiv) and its plain

ledger.note: c. 836: Philippopolis is incorporated under Malamir. 'the important city of Philippopolis (Plovdiv) was incorporated into the country.' The page gives no year; Omurtag died in 831 and Presian reigned from 836 (Presian page), so it falls in 831-836. The Omurtag page keeps Plovdiv outside the 815 border.

region.text: the Pannonian lands (Slavonia, Zagreb region) that Cliopatria's 840 shape no longer holds

ledger.note: 840: Cliopatria's shape drops the Slavonian and Pannonian land of 827-829. Page silent: the Omurtag page ends Bulgarian control there with no date and none of the pages opened records a Frankish reconquest; the Frankish dossier counts the same 125 cells as returned in 840.

region.text: 'most of Macedonia' to the Adriatic near Valona, with Kosovo and the Morava valley, as Cliopatria's 850 shape adds them

ledger.note: Presian's conquest of Macedonia, placed at 850: the main page says 'the Bulgarians took most of Macedonia', 'the borders of the country reached the Adriatic Sea near Valona' and 'as far south as the Rhodopes and the plain surrounding Thessaloniki' with no year. The Presian page: 'He ruled during an extensive expansion in Macedonia' (reign 836-852); 837 the Slavs near Thessalonica revolt and Isbul 'captured the city of Philippi'. Cliopatria's 850 shape adds Macedonia, Kosovo and the Morava lands.

region.text: 'a small area in Strandzha'; the radius is the researcher's

ledger.note: 852: at his accession Boris I 'threatened the Byzantines with an invasion' but did not attack and 'received a small area in Strandzha'.

region.text: Philippopolis (Plovdiv), the region of Zagora and the ports round the Gulf of Burgas

ledger.note: 855-856: the Byzantines under Michael III and Bardas strike back. Boris 'lost Philippopolis (Plovdiv), the region of Zagora, and the ports around the Gulf of Burgas'. Cliopatria's 860 shape does not draw this loss. The main page's 'the skilful diplomacy of Boris I prevented any territorial losses' contradicts the Boris page.

region.text: 'the region of Zagora'

ledger.note: 864: Boris buys peace with his conversion. 'Boris agreed to peace, promising conversion, in exchange for territorial concessions in Thrace'; he 'regained the region of Zagora recently recovered by the Byzantines' and was baptised secretly at Pliska in early 864. The Byzantine-Bulgarian wars page puts the return of Zagora in 863; the Boris page, which also dates the declaration of war to late 863, is followed. The page does not say Philippopolis or the Burgas ports came back.
893: the capital moves from Pliska to Preslav. An assembly 'moved the Bulgarian capital from Pliska to Preslav, to better cement the recent conversion'; infobox 'Preslav (893-968/972)'.

region.text: northern Dobruja

ledger.note: 895: the Magyars, allied with Byzantium, invade Bulgaria. 'Simeon's two encounters with the enemy in northern Dobruja resulted in Magyar victories'; an armistice with Byzantium followed 'towards the summer of 895'. The Hungarian-conquest page: the Hungarians 'forced Tzar Simeon to flee to the fortress of Dristra'.

region.text: northern Dobruja

ledger.note: 896: Simeon, with Pecheneg allies, 'defeating them completely' at the Southern Buh; the Magyars left Etelkoz for the Carpathian Basin.

region.text: the Black Sea steppe between the Danube delta and the Dnieper (Budjak, Bessarabia, Odessa, Mykolayiv, Kherson) that Cliopatria's 896 shape no longer holds

ledger.note: 896: Cliopatria's shape drops the Black Sea steppe north of the Danube delta. Page silent: no page opened says who held Budjak, Bessarabia and the Odessa steppe in 896. The Hungarian-conquest page has the Magyars invade Bulgaria and the Pechenegs then break into Hungarian lands from the east, undated; the Magyar dossier counts the same land as its gain. Pages for the Omurtag and Krum reigns give the Dnieper as Bulgaria's eastern limit.

region.text: 'an area between the Black Sea and Strandza'; the radius is the researcher's

ledger.note: 896: Bulgaria wins at Boulgarophygon (summer 896) and Byzantium pays tribute. 'the Byzantines also ceded an area between the Black Sea and Strandza to the Bulgarian Empire.' The Peter I page speaks of 'treaties of 897 and 904'. Cliopatria draws the area for 896-897 only; no page opened says it was given back.

region.text: the Black Sea steppe north of the Danube delta that Cliopatria's 898 shape holds again

ledger.note: 898: Cliopatria returns the steppe. The Hungarian-conquest page: 'The Bulgarians, according to Constantine Porphyrogenitus, attacked and routed the Hungarians' (undated). Page silent on 898.

region.text: Banat, Crisana and the plain to the Tisza that Cliopatria's 900 shape no longer holds

ledger.note: 900: Cliopatria's shape drops the Bulgarian lands beyond the Danube and Tisza (Banat, Transylvania, the plain to the Tisza). Page silent on Bulgarian rule there: the Hungarian-conquest page has Pannonia occupied 'in 900', 'intermittent' Bulgarian influence in Transylvania and the Great Hungarian Plain from c. 822, and 'Glad's army composed of Bulgarians, Vlachs and Pechenegs from Banat' (undated).

region.text: 'all Slavic-inhabited lands in modern southern Macedonia and southern Albania'; southern Macedonia is already inside the 900 shape

ledger.note: 904: Byzantium cedes the Slavic lands round Thessalonica. After the Arab seizure of Thessaloniki 'all Slavic-inhabited lands in modern southern Macedonia and southern Albania were ceded' and the border ran 'some 20 kilometres north of Thessaloniki'.

region.text: central and northern Albania, Raska and Kosovo that Cliopatria's 911 shape adds beyond the 904 cession

ledger.note: 911: Cliopatria's shape adds central and northern Albania, the Raska uplands and Kosovo. Page silent: the Simeon page says only that Bulgaria 'spread over a territory between the Aegean, the Adriatic and the Black seas' and names no western conquest before 917.

Late 913: Simeon is recognised as Emperor of the Bulgarians. 'Simeon's official recognition as Emperor of the Bulgarians by Patriarch Nicholas in the Blachernae Palace'; he took the title halfway through his reign. The state keeps its colour.

region.text: Thrace round Adrianople

ledger.note: 914: Simeon's war in Thrace. 'Simeon captured Adrianople, and Zoe later persuaded him to cede back Adrianople and withdraw his army'; 20 August 917 Achelous, then Katasyrtai; 922 Pigae. Cliopatria's shapes never include the Thracian conquests.

region.text: the principality of Petar Gojnikovic

ledger.note: 917: Simeon takes the Serbian prince. After Achelous and Katasyrtai 'Petar Gojnikovic was captured' and 'enchained and carried off to Bulgaria, where he died in a dungeon'. The year is the page's by sequence.

region.text: the Serbian principality

ledger.note: 924: Serbia is annexed. 'Bulgaria annexed Serbia directly.' Main page: 'ended with Bulgaria's annexation of Serbia at the end of that year.'

region.text: the whole Serbian principality

ledger.note: 924: Bulgaria annexes Serbia. 'Bulgaria annexed Serbia directly'; main page: 'In 924, the Serbs ambushed and defeated a small Bulgarian army' and the war 'ended with Bulgaria's annexation of Serbia at the end of that year.' Cliopatria's 926 shape is the 922 shape plus the Serbian principality's whole shape.

region.text: Tomislav's Croatia, the target of the invasion

ledger.note: 926: Alogobotur invades Croatia. 'In 926, Simeon's troops under Alogobotur invaded Croatia, at the time a Byzantine ally'; the main page: 'Further expansion in the Western Balkans was checked by King Tomislav of Croatia' who 'defeated a Bulgarian invasion in 926'. The pages name no place; the Croatian kingdom's own shape stands for the zone.

region.text: Tomislav's Croatia

ledger.note: 27 May 927: Simeon dies in Preslav and the Croatian front ends with him; the page gives no Croatian treaty.

region.text: Thrace round Adrianople

ledger.note: October 927: peace with Byzantium. 'As part of the peace treaty signed in October 927' the existing borders were confirmed; the Peter I page: 'Peace was obtained with the frontiers restored to those defined in treaties of 897 and 904', the tribute renewed and Peter's imperial title recognised. The Byzantine dossier counts a restoration of Thrace that Cliopatria's Bulgarian shapes never contained.

region.text: the Serbian principality

ledger.note: 933: Caslav frees Serbia. 'Caslav escaped the Bulgarian capital Preslav in 933 and, with tacit Byzantine support,' led a revolt; 'Serbia regained independence.' Cliopatria keeps Serbia in the Bulgarian shape to 935.

region.text: most of the Dobruja and the north-east of Bulgaria, as the Rus' invasion left them out of Cliopatria's 970 shape

ledger.note: August 967 or 968: the Rus' cross the Danube. 'In August 967 or 968, the Rus' crossed the Danube into Bulgarian territory' and 'occupied most of the Dobruja'; 'Sviatoslav seized 80 towns in northeastern Bulgaria' (not permanently occupied). Peter I page: 'some 80 Bulgarian fortresses in 968'. Preslav fell in summer 969 by context.

region.text: the part of the lost land that lies north of the Danube

ledger.note: 970: Cliopatria's 970 shape no longer holds the land north of the Danube (Muntenia, Budjak, Bessarabia, Odessa). Page silent: nothing opened says who held it after the Rus' invasion.

region.text: eastern Bulgaria: lower Moesia, Dobruja and the Thracian lands

ledger.note: 971: John Tzimiskes annexes eastern Bulgaria. 'the city was stormed on 13 April' (Preslav); 'Tzimiskes formally annexed Eastern Bulgaria to the Byzantine Empire.' The Byzantine-Bulgarian wars page: 'The Bulgarian lands in Thrace and lower Moesia now became part of the Byzantine Empire.' The main page: 'Although at the time the Byzantines controlled only the eastern regions of the country,' it was proclaimed a Byzantine province.

region.text: the north-east and Dobruja

ledger.note: Late July 971: the Rus' capitulate at Dorostolon. 'After the final and particularly savage battle in late July, the Rus' were forced to capitulate'; 'The Rus' army was allowed to depart'; the main page: 'compelled him to leave the Balkans in 971.'

972: the seat moves west to Skopje (infobox 'Preslav (893-968/972); Skopje (972-992)'). The Sviatoslav page has no capital move; the main page notes 'The lands to the west of the Iskar River remained free'.

region.text: the Oltenian part of the land lost between 970 and 980

ledger.note: c. 980: Cliopatria's shape drops Oltenia and the Danube lands of the Iron Gates. Page silent on the year: the Peter I page says only that the Magyars' settlement north of the Danube led to 'the eventual loss of the region to the Magyars', which happened after Peter's death.

region.text: Syrmia (Srem), the Serbian part of the land lost between 970 and 980

ledger.note: c. 980: Cliopatria's shape drops Syrmia (Srem) between the Sava and the Danube. Page silent: none of the pages opened mentions Belgrade or Syrmia after 971.

region.text: Epirus and 'the area of modern Durres'

ledger.note: 989: Samuel reaches the Adriatic. Bulgarian forces 'marched throughout Epirus' and 'seized the area of modern Durres' on the Adriatic; Samuel later appointed Ashot governor of Dyrrhachium.

region.text: 'the whole of Thessaly'

ledger.note: c. 990: Samuel holds Thessaly and Epirus. The main page says only that he went on 'annexing the whole of Thessaly and Epirus' (no year); the Samuel page has Larissa blockaded 'from 977 to 983'. Year taken from Cliopatria's 990 shape.

region.text: north-eastern Bulgaria with Pliska and Preslav, and Dobruja

ledger.note: 991: Moesia comes back to the Bulgarians. 'Although the titular emperor Roman of Bulgaria was captured in 991, Basil lost Moesia to the Bulgarians.' The main page: 'Samuel pushed east and recovered north-eastern Bulgaria, along with the old capitals, Pliska and Preslav.' The year is attached to Roman's capture, not to the loss; Cliopatria's shape shows the land from 990.
992: the seat moves from Skopje to Ohrid (infobox 'Ohrid (992-1015)'); the Samuel page: 'Samuel moved the capital from Skopje to Ohrid' without a year.

997: Samuel is proclaimed Emperor. After Roman died in captivity Samuel was 'chosen as the new Emperor of Bulgaria'; the main page: 'Samuel was proclaimed Emperor of Bulgaria.' The Cometopuli replace the house of Krum; the page calls the realm the 'Western Bulgarian Empire'.

region.text: Duklja, the principality of Jovan Vladimir

ledger.note: 998: Samuel crushes Duklja. 'Samuel launched a major campaign against the Duklja,' exiling Jovan Vladimir to Prespa, then went through Dalmatia and Croatia and 'northeast through Bosnia and Raska' before returning. The main page dates the capture of Jovan Vladimir to 997 ('took control of the Serb lands'). Cliopatria draws Montenegro in the Bulgarian shape from 990. Duklja needs its own dossier before 1056.

region.text: Syrmia (Srem)

ledger.note: c. 1000: Cliopatria's shape adds Syrmia. Page silent: the 998 campaign went 'northeast through Bosnia and Raska' but the page gives no annexation.

region.text: north-eastern Bulgaria with Preslav and Pliska, and Dobruja

ledger.note: 1000: Basil II's generals take the old capital. 'In 1000, the Byzantine generals Nikephoros Xiphias and Theodorokanos took the former Bulgarian capital Great Preslav'. The main page says 'In 1001 they seized Pliska and Preslav in the east'; the Samuel page: Basil's army 'recaptured Preslav and Pliska' in 1001 with north-eastern Bulgaria 'once again under Byzantine rule'.

region.text: Vodena (Edessa), Verrhoia (Veria) and Servia

ledger.note: 1001: Basil II retakes Macedonia from Thessalonica. 'In 1001, Basil, operating from Thessalonica, regained control of Vodena, Verrhoia and Servia.'

region.text: Macedonia and the Vardar route into Samuel's realm

ledger.note: 1002: the final war. 'In 1002, a full-scale war broke out' (Kleidion 29 July 1014; Basil 'completely conquered Bulgaria in 1018').

region.text: 'Thessalian towns'

ledger.note: 1001-1002: Basil's campaign 'later reconquered Thessalian towns in 1001-1002.'

region.text: Greek Epirus lost between the 1000 and 1003 shapes

ledger.note: 1003: Cliopatria's shape drops Epirus (Ipeiros). Page silent for Epirus; the Basil II page has Basil at Thessalonica in 1001 only.

region.text: the fortress and district of Vidin

ledger.note: 1003: Vidin falls. 'In 1003 ... Basil II besieged Vidin, and after an eight-month siege, the Byzantines ultimately captured the fortress' (Samuel page; the main page: 'in 1003 a major offensive along the Danube resulted in the fall of Vidin after an eight-month siege'). The Basil II page has the siege 'the following year' after 1001 and gives no year.

region.text: Skopje and its district

ledger.note: 1004: Skopje. 'in 1004 Basil II defeated Samuel in the battle of Skopje and took possession of the city.' The Samuel page: 'reached a key Bulgarian city, Skopje, in 1004' and beat the army at the Vardar crossing.

region.text: Dyrrhachium and its district

ledger.note: 1005: Dyrrhachium surrenders. 'In 1005, the governor of Dyrrhachium Ashot Taronites surrendered his city to the Byzantines.'

minus.text: the land lost between the 1003 and 1010 shapes

region.text: the Balkan part of the land lost between 1003 and 1010

ledger.note: c. 1010: Cliopatria's shape drops the rest of Samuel's southern realm: the Vardar and Pelagonian Macedonia, Epirus in Albania and Pcinja. Page silent between 1005 and 1014: the Basil II page says only that 'Bulgaria fought on for four more years' after Kleidion; the Samuel page names no place for 1005-1013.

region.text: the Iron Gates strip of Mehedinti

ledger.note: c. 1010: Cliopatria's shape hands the Iron Gates strip (Mehedinti) on the Danube to Hungary. Page silent; the Hungarian dossier counts the same cells as a gain in 1010 and withdraws them in 1015.
1015: Ohrid is taken and burned; Ivan Vladislav 'consolidated his positions in the mountains of Albania and Macedonia' and rebuilt Bitola from October 1015 (infobox 'Bitola (1015-1018)').

region.text: the Sofia basin, Plovdiv-Pazardzhik and the Danube plain that Cliopatria's 1015 shape no longer holds

ledger.note: 1015: Cliopatria's shape drops the Sofia basin, the upper Maritsa and the Danube plain from Vratsa to Lovech. Page silent on the places: the Ivan Vladislav page has Basil's 1015 campaign push Ivan 'back into the Albanian mountains' and an 88-day siege of Pernik in spring 1016 that 'was a failure'.

region.text: Macedonia and the Vardar route

ledger.note: 1018: the Bulgarian war ends. 'Bulgaria fought on for four more years, its resistance fired by Basil's cruelty, but it submitted in 1018.'

region.text: the remaining Bulgarian land from Ohrid and Bitola to the Albanian mountains

ledger.note: 1018: the last Bulgarian land passes to Basil II. 'In the early 1018 Ivan Vladislav besieged Dyrrhachium, but in February he was killed under the walls of the city'; 'the larger part of the Bulgarian nobility pledged loyalty to Basil II'; Krakra and the commanders of 35 castles surrendered at Serres; Ivan's son Presian and his brothers 'surrendered by the end of 1018'. Main page: 'By 1018, the last Bulgarian strongholds had surrendered'.

region.text: the whole remaining state, annexed as the theme of Bulgaria

ledger.note: 1018: the First Bulgarian Empire ends. 'Bulgaria was annexed by the Byzantine Empire'; infobox 'Theme Bulgaria established in Byzantine Empire: 1018'. Ivan Vladislav, last tsar, was killed at Dyrrhachium in February 1018.

wars.name: Battle of Ongal and the Byzantine-Bulgarian war of 680-681

zones.text: Moesia north of the Balkan Mountains

wars.outcome: Asparukh's Bulgars defeat Constantine IV's army at Ongal (680); in 681 the Byzantines sign a treaty ceding 'the territories to the north of the Balkan Mountains' and recognise the Bulgarian state.
wars.note: The Asparukh page spells the battle 'Ongala' and says the Byzantine Empire thereafter paid the Bulgars an annual tribute.

wars.name: Tervel's campaigns and the treaty of 716
wars.outcome: Tervel restores Justinian II (705) and receives Zagore; 'Skirmishes continued until 716 when Khan Tervel signed an important agreement with Byzantium that defined the borders'.

wars.name: Campaigns of Constantine V against Bulgaria
wars.outcome: Nine Byzantine campaigns, 756-775; the pages opened record no change of border.
wars.note: The page heads the section 755-775 and writes 'Between 756 and 775'.

wars.name: Krum's war on the Avars

zones.text: the Avar lands between the Danube and the Tisza

wars.outcome: The Avar Khaganate is destroyed ('Between 804 and 806 the Bulgarian armies thoroughly eliminated the Avar Khaganate'); Bulgaria borders the Franks on the middle Danube or the Tisza.
wars.note: The Krum page dates the defeat 'around 805'.

wars.name: Krum's war with Byzantium
wars.outcome: Krum wins the Struma valley (807), Serdica (809), Develt and Mesembria (812); Nikephoros I takes Pliska on 20 July 811 and is killed in the Varbitsa Pass (26 July); Versinikia 22 June 813 and the seizure of Adrianople; Omurtag's thirty-year peace of 815 fixes the border at Debeltos, the Erkesia trench and Kalugerovo.
wars.note: Krum himself died on 13 April 814, before the treaty.

wars.name: Omurtag's Frankish war and the Pannonian campaigns
wars.outcome: After the 818 Slavic revolt and failed talks (824-826, ultimatum 826), Omurtag's fleet on the Danube and the Drava in 827 'restored Bulgarian control over portions of southeastern Pannonia'; 'Similar events took place again in 829 with the same result.'
wars.note: The page does not name Ljudevit or the Pannonian Croats.

wars.name: Bulgarian-Serbian war of 839-842
wars.outcome: 'Presian invaded Serbian territory in 839'; the three years' war ended with Vlastimir victorious, Presian 'driven out of Serbian territory'. Bulgaria gained no land.
wars.note: The page ties its end to the death of Theophilos in 842.

wars.name: Bulgarian invasion of Serbia under Vladimir-Rasate
wars.outcome: Boris's son Vladimir-Rasate invaded Serbia; Mutimir's Serbs 'defeated the Bulgarians, capturing Vladimir and 12 boyars'. The Bulgarians kept nothing.

wars.name: Frankish and Croatian war on Bulgaria
wars.outcome: 'The Bulgarian-Slav campaign was a disaster, and Louis scored a great victory and invaded Bulgaria'; 'At the same time the Croats waged a war against the Bulgarians'; in 855 peace with Eastern Francia was restored.

wars.name: Byzantine reconquest of Thrace

zones.text: Philippopolis, Zagora and the Gulf of Burgas

wars.outcome: Michael III and Bardas take 'Philippopolis (Plovdiv), the region of Zagora, and the ports around the Gulf of Burgas'.

wars.name: Byzantine-Bulgarian war of 863-864
wars.outcome: Michael III declares war in late 863; Boris sues for peace, promises conversion, receives Zagora back in 864.
wars.note: The Byzantine-Bulgarian wars page puts the return of Zagora in 863.

wars.name: Bulgarian-Byzantine war of 894-896 with the Magyar invasion

zones.text: the area between the Black Sea and Strandza

wars.outcome: Over a trade dispute Simeon invades Byzantium; the Byzantines bring in the Magyars, who win in northern Dobruja (895); Simeon and the Pechenegs destroy them at the Southern Buh (896) and he annihilates the Byzantine army at Boulgarophygon; the peace brings tribute and the Black Sea-Strandza area.

wars.name: Byzantine-Bulgarian war of 913-927
wars.outcome: Simeon crowned emperor (913); Adrianople taken 914 and ceded back; Achelous (20 August 917); Katasyrtai; Thessaly to the Isthmus of Corinth (920-922); Pigae (922); truce on the Golden Horn (9 September 924); peace in October 927 confirming the existing borders.
wars.note: The main page adds the seizure of Thebes, which the Simeon page does not mention.

wars.name: Bulgarian conquest of Serbia
wars.outcome: Petar Gojnikovic is taken to Bulgaria (917); 'Bulgaria annexed Serbia directly' in 924.

wars.name: Bulgarian-Croatian war of 926
wars.outcome: Alogobotur invades Croatia and Tomislav defeats the invasion; Bulgaria gains nothing.
wars.note: The pages opened name no battlefield.

wars.name: Rus' invasion of Bulgaria and John Tzimiskes' campaign
wars.outcome: Sviatoslav takes the Dobruja and 80 towns (968), Preslav and Boris II (969); Tzimiskes storms Preslav on 13 April 971 and the Rus' capitulate at Dorostolon in late July; eastern Bulgaria is annexed.
wars.note: Peter I abdicated in 969 and died 30 January 970 (Peter I page).

wars.name: Basil II's Sredets campaign and the Gates of Trajan
wars.outcome: Basil II besieges Sredets in 986 and withdraws when the Bulgarians burn his siege equipment; on 17 August 986 his army is 'ambushed and routed at the Trajan's Gates Pass'.

wars.name: Samuel's raid on Thessaly and the Peloponnese; Spercheios
wars.outcome: Samuel defeats the Byzantines at Thessaloniki, marches through Thessaly and 'entered the Peloponnese, devastating everything'; the Byzantines rout the Bulgarians at the Spercheios on 19 July 996 and Samuel is wounded.
wars.note: No land is held in the Peloponnese.

wars.name: Samuel's Duklja campaign
wars.outcome: Samuel captures Jovan Vladimir and takes 'the Serb lands' (997, main page) or sends him to Prespa in a campaign through Dalmatia, Croatia, Bosnia and Raska (998, Samuel page).

wars.name: Basil II's conquest of Bulgaria
wars.outcome: 'In 1002, a full-scale war broke out': Vidin (1003), Skopje (1004), Dyrrhachium (1005), Kleidion (29 July 1014), Samuel's death (6 October 1014), Ohrid (1015), Pernik (1016 siege failed), Ivan Vladislav killed at Dyrrhachium (February 1018); the nobility submit and Bulgaria is annexed.
wars.note: The Byzantine-Bulgarian wars page calls the blinding of 14,000 prisoners 'a later invention'.

certainty.note: The Balkan-Mountains and Thracian frontier is approximate before the 815 line; the 716 agreement 'defined the borders' but the page names no line; the steppe frontier to the Dnieper is soft throughout and unverified before 803.

The Thracian frontier from Debeltos along the Erkesia trench to the Maritsa at Kalugerovo is a treaty line (815) and the Frankish frontier on the middle Danube is 'firmly settled' by 827, but the shapes keep the whole outline soft; the Macedonian, Serbian and steppe frontiers are approximate.
Only the 904 line 'some 20 kilometres north of Thessaloniki' is a stated frontier; the western, Serbian and Thracian fronts moved with the war.
The Byzantine frontier is the one 'restored to those defined in treaties of 897 and 904' in 927; the Serbian, Magyar and Pecheneg frontiers are approximate.
Rus' occupation, Byzantine annexation and Basil II's campaigns leave no stated lines; every frontier is approximate.

notes:
Dossier written 2026-11-01 from 14 pages (the page budget). Cliopatria row 'First Bulgarian Empire' 682..1017, 31 shapes, kept as one state; the 1018 end and the 681 start come from the pages and are added as new keyframes (681, 1018), together with 856-863 (Boris's losses), 904-910 (the Thessaloniki cession), 925 and 933-935 (Serbia).
Cliopatria checks: the first shape (682) contains Old Great Bulgaria's last shape (674-681; 246 of its 248 cells), so the steppe to the Dnieper is inherited, not read from a page; no page opened gives it for 682-805. The 830 shape reaches Zagreb and Banja Luka, more than 'portions of southeastern Pannonia'. The shape for 926-935 is the 922 shape plus the whole Serbian principality. The 1015 shape omits Sofia and Pernik, which held out in 1016; corrected by a Pernik circle. Cliopatria never draws Simeon's Thracian conquests, the 855-856 losses or the Rus' occupation; they are carried by the contest, loss and occupation events.
Disagreements between pages: Zagore returns in 863 (wars page) or 864 (Boris page, followed); Preslav and Pliska fall in 1000 (Basil II page, followed) or 1001 (main and Samuel pages); Duklja falls in 997 (main page) or 998 (Samuel page); the main page has Boris I prevent 'any territorial losses' while the Boris page has the 855-856 losses; the main page has Simeon take Thebes, which the Simeon page does not mention; the 896 peace (Simeon page) against 'treaties of 897 and 904' (Peter I page); Vidin falls in 1003 (Samuel page) or the year after 1001 (Basil II page).
Events at confidence 1 (page silent, shape-led): 825, 840, 850, 896 (steppe), 898, 900, 911, 970 (north bank), 980 (two), 990, 1000, 1003 (Epirus), 1010 (two), 1015. They record Cliopatria's shape changes against the nearest dated page and are the gaps for a gap-filler.
Counterparts that need dossiers or matching entries: Duklja before 1056 (Principality of Duklja; suggested slug principality-of-duklja); the Magyar and Hungarian dossiers should carry the gains at 896/900 (steppe, Banat, Transylvania) and 980 (Oltenia) that this dossier records as losses; the Hungarian dossier counts the Iron Gates strip in 1010. Slavic tribes (Timocani, Abodrites, Braničevci) are 'nobody'.
Not settled: the Cometopuli in 976-997 (the pages opened date only 976 and Roman's capture in 991); the ruler strip has no names between 721 and 777 and between 971 and 997 except Boris II; Malamir's dates are derived. Gazetteer: all names used exist except none needed; 'Pannonia' is absent from regions.jsonl and was avoided (shape differences and Slavonia are used instead).
